vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mma-bridge
Version: 1.2.0

The mma-bridge skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the Meteor Master AI (MMA) software, providing a CLI-based bridge to interact with the application's local API. The skill includes instructions for checking installation via PowerShell, starting the application, and querying meteor detection data using the `mma-bridge` tool. All documented behaviors, such as file exports and local network requests to 127.0.0.1, are consistent with the stated purpose of managing meteor monitoring data and do not show signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only guide for using a local mma-bridge CLI to talk to a local Meteor Master AI application; its requirements and actions are coherent with that purpose, with one minor metadata omission (the skill actually depends on a CLI that the registry metadata did not declare).

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md clearly describes interacting with a local mma-bridge CLI and a local Meteor Master AI (MMA) app. However the registry metadata claims 'no required binaries' while the instructions require the mma CLI (via `npm install mma-bridge -g`) and a locally installed Meteor Master AI app. This is a metadata omission but not a functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to checking/starting/listing local MMA instances, reading a temp/registry directory, and sending HTTP requests to localhost ports (e.g., /health) or invoking the mma CLI (mma post). The instructions do not instruct the agent to read unrelated system secrets or exfiltrate data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec). SKILL.md recommends installing `mma-bridge` via `npm install -g`, which means the user will install a third-party npm package; the registry did not provide an install spec or provenance. Instruction-only status reduces platform install risk, but installing an external npm package from an unknown publisher is a separate operational risk the user should evaluate.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables and does not request credentials. It works with local files, temp directories, and localhost service ports, which are proportional to the stated purpose of controlling a local MMA application. Example data includes an RTSP URL with credentials — those are examples and not requested by the skill, but users should avoid pasting real secrets into commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent/always-on privileges (always:false). It does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings in the provided instructions. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but is not excessive here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an instructions-only adapter for a local CLI (mma-bridge) and a locally installed Meteor Master AI app. Before installing/using: 1) Confirm you actually want to install the `mma-bridge` npm package and verify its publisher and source on the npm registry (running `npm install -g` from an unknown package is a risk). 2) Understand the skill will list and query local MMA instances, read files in your temp directory, and call localhost HTTP endpoints (ports like 9000); these actions are expected for this use case. 3) Do not paste real credentials into example commands (RTSP examples include credentials). 4) If you are concerned, run the npm package in a sandboxed environment or inspect the package code before installing. The registry metadata should ideally declare the mma binary dependency — treat that omission as a documentation gap rather than malicious behavior.
